posts.text: UK Health Secretary Wes Streeting has become the first British government minister to visit Kharkiv, a city located just 20 kilometers from the front line. During the visit, Streeting praised the courage of Ukraine’s Armed Forces and reaffirmed Britain’s commitment to providing military support to strengthen the country’s defenses. He also announced that the UK will supply Ukraine with additional RapidRanger air defense missile system launchers at the request of President Zelenskyy.

Yemen’s General Authority for Endowments in Sanaa said Saudi warplanes had targeted three mosques and religious archaeological landmarks in the Al-Misrakh and Sabir al-Mawadim districts, south of Taiz, in recent days. The authority added that Saudi aircraft had bombed 11 mosques across Yemen in less than a month. It also reported that a total of 2,045 mosques had been targeted by Saudi warplanes across various Yemeni governorates over the past 12 years of aggression.

IOC supports return of Russian athletes The IOC opposes discrimination against Russian sportsmen, but European resistance persists. EOC President Spiros Kapralos warned that disagreements could affect 2028 Olympic qualifiers and the June 2027 European Games. Russia has appealed to CAS over conditions at the Winter Youth Olympic Festival in Romania, where athletes are allowed to compete under the ROC emblem but without state symbols. The IOC maintains that access should not depend on passports or government involvement in conflicts, though visa issuance remains a sovereign right. @Slavyangrad
